headline: 7 men sentenced to death for gang-rape of woman in Jamalpur
summary: A Jamalpur court has delivered the death penalty to seven convicts in a case involving the abduction and gang-rape of a woman last year.
details: A Jamalpur court has sentenced seven men to death for the abduction and gang-rape of a woman in Bakshiganj upazila last year.
The verdict was delivered by Judge Muhammad Abdur Rahim of the Jamalpur Women and Children Repression Prevention Tribunal-1.
The convicts are Md Rashedur Rahman alias Pappu, Md Biju Mia, Md Badsha Mia, Md Jewel Mia, Md Ashraful Islam, Jasim, and Asmat.
Another accused, Md Idris Ali, was acquitted by the tribunal as the charges against him could not be proved.
According to case documents, the victim was abducted from the Nilakshiya area of Bakshiganj on the night of May 25, 2025, and taken to an abandoned house where she was raped.
Following the incident, the victim filed a case with Bakshiganj Police Station under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act.
caption:
Seven men have been sentenced to death for the abduction and gang-rape of a woman in Jamalpur.

A Jamalpur court has sentenced seven men to death for the abduction and gang-rape of a woman in Bakshiganj upazila last year.

The verdict was delivered by Judge Muhammad Abdur Rahim of the Jamalpur Women and Children Repression Prevention Tribunal-1.

The convicts are Md Rashedur Rahman alias Pappu, Md Biju Mia, Md Badsha Mia, Md Jewel Mia, Md Ashraful Islam, Jasim, and Asmat.

Another accused, Md Idris Ali, was acquitted by the tribunal as the charges against him could not be proved.

According to case documents, the victim was abducted from the Nilakshiya area of Bakshiganj on the night of May 25, 2025, and taken to an abandoned house where she was raped.

Following the incident, the victim filed a case with Bakshiganj Police Station under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act.

headline: June electricity bills: Most complaints are due to misunderstandings
summary: State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Anindya Islam Amit says higher bills are primarily due to increased usage and tariff hikes, not system errors.
details: State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Anindya Islam Amit stated that most complaints regarding June electricity bills were caused by misunderstandings and have since been resolved.

The Power Division explains that the increase in bills was not only due to tariff hikes but also a significant increase in electricity consumption. For residential users, higher usage often leads to higher tariff slabs, resulting in higher total bills.

The Power Division also noted that some clerical errors were found in a few cases, which are being corrected. Secretary Mirana Mahrukh highlighted that many 'ghost bills' were verified and found to be correct based on usage and price increases.

Regarding load shedding in rural areas, the Minister mentioned that decentralization has not yet been achieved, leading to disparities. He attributed the current crisis in the power sector to the 'wrong policies' of the previous fascist government, blaming excessive capacity payments to private companies.
The government is now focusing on renewable energy, aiming to achieve a capacity of at least 10,000 MW of electricity production from renewable sources by the end of its term.

PDB Chairman Rezaul Karim explained that the World Cup and extreme heatwaves, along with exams, have increased demand. He added that peaking power plants are being used more at night to meet this surge in demand.

State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Anindya Islam Amit stated that most complaints regarding June electricity bills were caused by misunderstandings and have since been resolved.
